$about: capability -> the code globs that must move with its spec (R11). Copy this to specs/capability-map.json and replace the capabilities with yours.
Keys starting with $ are metadata rather than capabilities: this note, and $unclaimed below.

The paths are the paved monorepo shape - apps/* for anything deployed, packages/* for what is never deployed on its own. A single-package repo writes src/** and has no packages; the mechanism is identical.

Glob syntax: * stays inside one path segment; ** spans any number of segments including none, so apps/*/src/**/payment/** covers apps/api/src/payment/capture.ts as well as apps/api/src/routes/v2/payment/capture.ts.

A glob starting with ! excludes: the capability claims what its other globs match except those paths. That is how a sibling capability living inside an already-claimed folder gets its own coupling - see refunds below - instead of every edit demanding both specs. An exclusion narrows a claim and cannot replace one, and spec-guard --audit reports a file it hands to nobody.

An entry may instead be { external: <repo>, reason: <why> } when the capability's implementation lives in a repository this one does not own - a plugin, a satellite rules_* repo, a vendor SDK. No glob here can reach that code, so nothing is enforced for it; the capability still has a spec here, and --audit names every external binding on every run so the hatch cannot widen quietly.

channel-sync.reason: each channel's connector is released from its own repository; this repo holds the contract and the spec, not the implementations
